items.summary: How many times have you heard someone say "I don’t get into politics. I just focus on my career" Or when there are protests, you hear people ask, "Why does everything have to be politicized?" It may sound balanced. But let us be honest for a second. Every week on Let Me Explain , we break down complex things—a law, a court judgment, or a government policy. But today, I want to make a simple submission. items.title: Only Supreme Court can say its judgment will not be cited as precedent: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that only the Supreme Court can give a caveat that its judgment will not be cited as a precedent. A Division Bench of Justices C Hari Shankar and Vinod Kumar said that such a power is not available to any other court. “This caveat is, therefore, unique to the Supreme Court, as its decisions are constitutionally binding by virtue of Article 141 of the Constitution of India,” the Bench explained. It said that even if the facts of a case are similar to those in an earlier Supreme Court judgment, a lower court cannot treat that judgment as binding precedent if the Supreme Court itself has clarified that it should not apply in such circumstances. In such cases, the binding effect of Article 141 of the Constitution would not apply. Further, the Bench reasoned that if other courts say that their judgments will not be cited as a precedent, it could result in a situation in which similarly placed litigants would receive different treatment. “Ex facie, this would be impermissible,” the Court added. items.title: Chennai rains: T Nagar, Velachery and other areas face waterlogging
items.summary: Heavy intermittent rainfall since Tuesday night, October 20, has caused waterlogging in several Chennai neighbourhoods, including T Nagar, Velachery, Nungambakkam, Ashok Nagar, and West Mambalam. The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has deployed motor pumps, tractors, and other machinery to remove stagnant rainwater. Civic workers have also been working on clearing blockages in drains and directing the water into the stormwater drain network. In T Nagar, rainwater accumulated on several major roads, including Panagal Park Road and Habibullah Road, as well as streets adjoining Thirumalai Road. Panagal Park Road, an important stretch connecting Anna Salai to T Nagar, was severely waterlogged. Two-wheelers, buses, autorickshaws, and cars struggled to navigate the road, with water reaching halfway up some vehicles. Traffic along this stretch has also been affected by ongoing Metro Rail construction on one side and stormwater drain works on the other. Bazullah Road and streets adjoining Thirumalai Road were also affected. Waterlogging was reported on GN Chetty Road too, where infrastructure works had been undertaken under the Smart City project. items.title: Telangana CM Revanth hikes ex gratia for families of police personnel killed on duty
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Wednesday, October 21, announced an increase in ex-gratia payments for families of police personnel killed in the line of duty. Speaking at the Police Martyrs Memorial in Goshamahal, CM Revanth directed Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand to increase the ex-gratia payment for the families of Home Guards from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh. The ex-gratia amount for families of Superintendents of Police (SPs) and IPS officers was increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 2 crore, while the ex-gratia amount for families of head constables and Additional SPs will be between Rs 1 crore and Rs 1.5 crore, compared with the Rs 45 lakh they received earlier. “The increase was not merely financial assistance but is a marker of respect for the families of the martyrs,” CM Revanth said. He also announced that all vacant posts in the state police department would be filled by 2028.
